Class ColumnsElement

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<ColumnsElement>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.ContainerElement<ColumnsElement>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.elements.ColumnsElement
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
public final class ColumnsElement extends ContainerElement<ColumnsElement>
A multi-column grid layout container that arranges children into columns.

The column count is auto-calculated from the available width and the maximum preferred width of children, or can be set explicitly via columnCount(int).

Items can be ordered row-first (default) or column-first:

  • Row-first: items fill left-to-right, then top-to-bottom (like reading text)
  • Column-first: items fill top-to-bottom, then left-to-right (like newspaper columns)

All layout properties can be set via CSS or programmatically. Programmatic values override CSS values when both are set.

Supported CSS properties:

  • flex — "start", "center", "end", "space-between", "space-around", "space-evenly"
  • spacing — gap between columns in cells
  • margin — margin around the columns
  • column-count — explicit number of columns
  • column-order — "row-first" or "column-first"

Example usage: 

columns(text("A"), text("B"), text("C"), text("D")).columnCount(2).spacing(1)

    • preferredSize

      public Size preferredSize(int availableWidth, int availableHeight, RenderContext context)
      Description copied from interface: Element
      Returns the preferred size of this element.

      The availableWidth/Height parameters allow elements to adapt their dimensions based on constraints. Use -1 for unconstrained.

      Common patterns:

      • Text elements: height depends on width (text wrapping)
      • Aspect-ratio elements: both dimensions interrelated
      • Fixed elements: ignore available dimensions

      Return value semantics:

      • Positive values = known size (use as constraint)
      • Zero = explicitly zero-sized (element should collapse)
      • Negative (-1) = unknown size (element should fill available space)
      Parameters:
      availableWidth - the available width in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      availableHeight - the available height in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      context - the render context for CSS resolution, may be null
      Returns:
      the preferred size
